Back Tap listing copy is not AssistiveTouch, custom keyboard, Guided Access, or Control Center

Accessibility marketing apps blur several surfaces indie teams conflate. AppLocale covers listing metadata only — Back Tap trigger marketing on the product page:

Back Tap-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Back Tap marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Back Tap assignment — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Back Tap vs 轻点背面 vs 背部轻点

US pages use "Back Tap", "Double Tap Back", "Triple Tap Back", or "Tap Back." China storefront copy often uses 轻点背面 for the Accessibility setting, 轻点两下背面 or 轻点三下背面 for double- or triple-tap assignment, or 背部轻点 when describing the physical gesture — depending on whether you mean Shortcut assignment, screenshot trigger, or accessibility companion badges. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual Back Tap scope.

Double Tap Back vs Triple Tap Back vs Back Tap shortcut

Screenshot galleries often label three distinct flows: Settings → Accessibility → Touch → Back Tap walkthrough (在设置中分配轻点背面), Double Tap Back Shortcut demo (轻点两下背面运行快捷指令), and Triple Tap Back action badge (轻点三下背面). These signal assignment intent, two-tap vs three-tap mapping, and Shortcut picker context — different from AssistiveTouch menu demos or custom keyboard install screens. Match the trigger model your English listing and screenshots actually show.

Assign to Back Tap vs Works with Back Tap

Some apps badge "Assign to Back Tap" on gallery frames; others use "Works with Back Tap" when they expose a Shortcut users map manually. Listing copy should distinguish assignment walkthrough language (分配至轻点背面) from compatibility badges (支持轻点背面) unless your English page already makes that scope clear. AppLocale rewrites from your source — we do not assign Back Tap on the buyer's device.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need Back Tap search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 轻点背面, 轻点两下背面, 背部轻点, and Back Tap 快捷指令 each signal different intent from generic 快捷指令 keywords alone.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Assign to Back Tap" headlines on gallery frames — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

AppLocale FAQ

Does AppLocale implement Back Tap detection or UIAccessibility?

No. We deliver Connect listing metadata copy only — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot caption lines. UIAccessibility APIs, Back Tap detection, Core Motion, private API workarounds, AssistiveTouch menu engineering, and Shortcut runtime implementation are outside scope.

How is Back Tap listing copy different from AssistiveTouch, custom keyboard, Guided Access, or Control Center?

Back Tap listing copy covers a double or triple tap on the back of iPhone mapped to a Shortcut or system action under Settings → Accessibility → Touch → Back Tap. AssistiveTouch covers the on-screen assistive menu — not tapping the device back. Custom keyboard listing copy covers a keyboard extension under Settings → General → Keyboard. Guided Access listing copy covers single-app lock. Control Center listing copy covers the system tray — Back Tap may open it, but that is a trigger assignment, not Control Center toggle marketing as the lead. Those are separate scopes with different screenshot vocabulary.

Should my zh-Hans listing claim my app IS Back Tap?

No. Apple ships Back Tap as a system Accessibility feature; third-party apps expose Shortcuts or workflows users assign to it. AppLocale rewrites from your source claims — we do not invent system-feature replacement, private Back Tap detection, or certify Accessibility review.

No. Back Tap assignment happens in Settings on the user's iPhone. Shortcut actions and in-app workflows come from your binary and iOS — not Connect listing fields. AppLocale covers product-page marketing copy only.
